Title: Diagnosis
Details: The test failure and current bug report indicate an issue with selecting nodes via XPath expressions involving the root node using the descendant-or-self axis (//root/@id/text()). The bug report describes that JXPath returns null instead of the expected attribute value "1234".

Tracing from JXPathContext.selectSingleNode(String xpath), the method attempts to get a Pointer from getPointer(xpath). The getPointer(String xpath) is implemented in JXPathContextReferenceImpl.getPointer(String xpath), which compiles the XPath expression and then calls getPointer(String xpath, Expression expr).

In getPointer(String xpath, Expression expr), the compiled expression is evaluated using expr.computeValue(getEvalContext()). If the result is an EvalContext, it retrieves getSingleNodePointer(), and if a Pointer, further checks if it is actual (existing node). Otherwise, it creates a new NodePointer.

The problem likely originates from expression evaluation or from how the root node is handled in the evaluation context or node pointer creation for descendant-or-self axes starting at the root. The returned Pointer may be null or non-actual if the root node isn't properly considered during descendant axis evaluation, leading to null returned by selectSingleNode.

The recent bug reports do not mention XPath root node or descendant axis directly, so they are not immediately relevant.

The root cause is that the evaluation logic in org.apache.commons.jxpath.ri.JXPathContextReferenceImpl.getPointer() or the expression evaluation (computeValue in Expression) does not correctly handle descendant-or-self axes when starting from the root node, thus failing to find root node attributes like in the XPath //root/@id/text() and causing the testGetNode() to fail when selecting nodes by XPath //vendor (which also uses descendant axis).

Next, investigating the handling of getSingleNodePointer() in EvalContext and how node pointers treat axes, especially for the root node and its descendants will be important for fixing this.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
